messages:
jess (Support): @ops-lead escalating: AcmeCorp reporting P99 latency ~12s for inference during their nightly billing window. They hit 500s and timeouts; they say it started ~23:05 UTC. Customer very upset, asked for ETA. :rotating_light:
omar (SRE): Can you paste the customer request IDs or example request body? Need to correlate traces.
maria (Oncall): I grabbed traces for the time range. p95 jumped modestly but p99 exploded. Looks like a scale-up gap + a bunch of attach failures (auth 401s) and image-pull delays.
jess (Support): Customer provided one request id: req_0a1b2c3d. Payload is a moderate-length chat with system prompt + 1024 tokens.
omar (SRE): OK pulling logs for req_0a1b2c3d...
deploy-bot: new deploy to prod-channel at 2026-03-16T22:58:00Z by deploy-bot (image: inference-runtime:v2.14.0)
kai (Eng Platform): Noted. Recent deploy changed the autoscaler backoff behavior (longer attach retries). Could be related.
omar (SRE): From the attach logs: several attach attempts timed out at the provisioner; backend returned 503s while nodes were spinning up. Also saw a cold GPU init stall where model cache download took 55s.
jess (Support): Customer also said they saw intermittent auth 401s during the spike.
maria (Oncall): Auth 401s look like KMS token refresh storms during billing window — lots of clients renewing simultaneously hitting auth DB. That increases attach failure rate which cascades into scale-up queue.
ops-lead: We need a mitigation plan to calm customer's p99 ASAP and a repro for the eng team. Quick mitigations?
kai (Eng Platform): Short-term: 1) Move AcmeCorp to a higher-priority pool (if they have reserved capacity) or route to hosted fallback, 2) bump their min_pool for the billing window, 3) patch autoscaler backoff to allow faster attach concurrency.
omar (SRE): Also recommend manual prewarm of N GPUs and attach to the pool for the window. I can trigger warmup for +4 GPUs for Acme.
jess (Support): I'll offer the customer fallback routing + ETA for prewarm.
alex (Customer): Appreciate quick action. Can you reproduce or explain root cause? This started after you rolled out the change earlier today.
kai (Eng Platform): Likely a combination: deploy changed autoscaler retry/backoff; auth token refresh spike increased error surface; image/model cache pulls slowed cold starts. Combined -> scale-up queue pileup -> p99 blowup. Repro steps below.
omar (SRE): Repro steps (internal):
```
# repro script (dev env)
# 1) Simulate 200 concurrent requests at billing window rate
ab -n 200 -c 50 -p sample_payload.json -T application/json https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
# 2) Temporarily flip autoscaler backoff config to slower/shorter in control plane
# 3) Throttle auth mock to return intermittent 401s at 5% error rate
# Observe: attach queue length and attach_time p99 spike -> request timeouts
```
ops-lead: Good. Please capture the following metrics for the incident timeline: attach_queue_length, attach_time_p95/p99, model_cache_download_time, auth_401_rate, pool_active_gpus, image_pull_failures.
maria (Oncall): I have a Grafana link with those panels: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/scaleup/attach-metrics?orgId=1&from=now-2h&to=now
omar (SRE): From the logs: model cache download for that model (gptx-8b-quant) hit the S3 throttling threshold. S3 rate limits caused the long cold init. Suggest we add per-model cache concurrency limits and a local CDN cache for the hot billing-window models.
kai (Eng Platform): Longer-term: add jitter/randomized auth token refresh schedule for clients, add prewarming schedule for priority customers, and implement fast-path fallback to a lightweight quantized variant when cache cold.
jess (Support): Immediate playbook I'm going to run now: 1) Offer customer hosted-fallback routing for next 3 hours, 2) Schedule manual +4 GPU prewarm for their region, 3) Patch autoscaler backoff to reduce retry backoff for 30m, 4) Notify customer with ETA ~20m. I'll update here when done.
omar (SRE): I can trigger prewarm and push a hot-cache snapshot to the pool to reduce model init to <5s. Will ping when live.
ops-lead: Also open a post-incident ticket for config change that rolled earlier. We need rollback + canary gating for autoscaler param changes.
alex (Customer): Thanks. After the fallback was enabled I see p99 drop to ~900ms. Good to keep that while you investigate root cause.
jess (Support): Confirming we enabled fallback routing at 23:18 UTC, prewarm started 23:20 UTC. Customer confirms improved.
maria (Oncall): Postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause (deploy param + auth storm + S3 throttling), mitigations performed, follow-ups (prewarm schedule, autoscaler gating, auth refresh jitter, per-model cache limits).
ops-lead: Assign follow-ups: kai to autoscaler gating PR, mar to auth jitter design, omar to cache/concurrency limit changes, jess to customer debrief.
kai (Eng Platform): I'll open PR for autoscaler gating and add canary flag. ETA EOD.
omar (SRE): Opening incident ticket 2026-03-16-ACME-P99-001 with full logs/traces and repro steps.
jess (Support): Customer debrief sent, they requested a summary and the playbook actions. I'll attach the incident ticket.
alex (Customer): Appreciate the transparency. Please add a contact window so we can escalate directly if we see a reoccurence.
ops-lead: Add dedicated Slack escalation alias for priority customers.
deploy-bot: incident ticket created: #2026-03-16-ACME-P99-001
